name: God module
definition: A module owns responsibilities that change for different reasons.
evidence: Trace distinct responsibilities, their dependencies and concrete changes.
counterexample: A large cohesive implementation behind a small interface can be appropriate.

name: Shotgun surgery
definition: One concept change requires edits across many modules.
evidence: Show a real change and the duplicated knowledge at its edit sites.
counterexample: A deliberate cross-layer feature can need several legitimate edits.

name: Shallow module
definition: The interface makes callers learn nearly as much complexity as the implementation hides.
evidence: Inspect caller obligations and apply the deletion test.
counterexample: A small adapter can isolate a dependency or enforce a useful invariant.

name: Leaky interface
definition: Callers must understand implementation details to use a module correctly.
evidence: Identify repeated ordering, configuration or error-handling obligations.
counterexample: A domain invariant in an explicit interface is not an implementation leak.

name: Contradictory state
definition: The state shape permits combinations the domain cannot accept.
evidence: Trace a reachable invalid combination and the guards that repair it.
counterexample: Several independent fields may represent legitimately independent state.

name: Effect chain
definition: Effects derive or synchronize React state that could be computed without that synchronization.
evidence: Trace each state dependency and identify the external system, if any.
counterexample: An Effect that synchronizes with an external system can be necessary.

name: Unbounded work
definition: A result set, retry sequence or concurrent task collection lacks an effective limit.
evidence: Follow the complete path and account for infrastructure and caller limits.
counterexample: A validated finite dataset or enforced upstream limit can bound the operation.

name: Swallowed failure
definition: A failed operation becomes success or disappears without an actionable result.
evidence: Trace the failure through its consumer and show the misleading outcome.
counterexample: An intentional best-effort operation may return an explicit partial result.

name: Duplicated domain rule
definition: Several modules independently encode the same decision and can disagree.
evidence: Compare the rule and a real or plausible divergence in its consumers.
counterexample: Similar code can describe different domain rules and should stay separate.

name: Change hotspot
definition: An area repeatedly touched by development; a review priority signal.
evidence: Inspect recent history and the reasons for change.
counterexample: Frequent changes alone do not prove a code smell.
